page.layout: One column of running text, full width. Left margin: three notes beside the paragraphs (Græcorum philosophorum catalogus with Greek line; Fabulæ poëtarum qui enarrandæ?; Septem Græciæ sapientes.). Bottom right: catchword.

main_text.p: Atq; hi sunt authores & cultores philosophia Ori-entales, iuque cum sacri, Hebraei scilicet, tum pro-fani, Chaldaei, Magi Persarum, Gymnosophistæ & Brachmanes Indorum, de quibus Strabo lib.15. & Bardesanes Babylonius; Sacerdotes denique Ægyptiorum: sequuntur Occidentales, iuque tum Græci, tum Latini. Nihil enim hic attinet dicere de philosophis Gallia, qui Druides appellan-tur.

Græci philosophiæ inventores & cultores fuerunt veteres tum poëtæ, tum philosophi. Græcorum philosophorum catalogus [illegible, ~10 letters] [illegible, ~5 letters]Poëtæ fuerunt Linus, Orpheus, Musæus, Homerus, Hesiodus, &c. qui odas & hymnos cecinerunt, cum dulces, tum sapienter conscripti. Fabulæ poë-tarum qui enarrandæ?Hi involucris fabularum quamplurima texerunt scitu digna. Proinde illorum fabulæ enarrandæ sunt physicè, ethicè, politicè; ut ostendit Natalis Comes in suâ Mythologiâ. Priscos illos poëtas indubiè imitati sunt Talmudistæ, qui multa habent fabulosa, si ῥητὸν spectes; at si διάνοιαν & ἐπιμύ-θιον, innumera ista pallio poetico tecta sunt arcana de rerum naturis. Eam ob causam poemata olim magno erant in honore. Et Plato in Lyside scribit, poëtas fuisse veteribus instar patrum & ducum sapientiæ. Unde a quibusdam salutantur ethnicorum hierophantæ.

Septem Græciæ sapientes.Post veteres illos poëtas efflorueruntse-ptem sapientes, eorumq; discipuli, à quibus ortæ duæ sectæ & scholæ, Italica, à Pythagorâ, primo nominis philosophici inventore constituta, & Mathematicis maximè de-dita: & Ionica à Thalete Milesio, Sapientum

page.notes: Running head and page number as printed. The Greek line of the first left-margin note (after "catalogus") could not be read letter by letter, so it is marked illegible. The Greek in the text, "ῥητὸν" after "si", is read with some doubt. The mark between "Plato" and "in" is taken as a stroke, not a letter. "Atq;" is read with a doubtful abbreviation mark. The catchword "unq" is copied as printed. Running head spacing in "ARCHILOGIÆ" is typographic and copied without spacing.
